ideas.idea: SmartMoving-native outbound lead engine for independent moving companies
ideas.description: An outbound lead-generation service for residential moving companies. It monitors newly listed homes, finds and verifies each seller’s contact details, sends personalized outreach on the mover’s behalf, and routes interested replies directly into SmartMoving. The proposed version would sell smaller exclusive ZIP-code territories with done-for-you onboarding.
ideas.traction: $7,615 MRR from 8 active subscriptions (TrustMRR snapshot at time of research) | 17 Oct 2026 authenticated: $0 MRR, 0 active subscriptions; $300 30-day revenue; $144,034 all-time; -100% MRR 30d change. CRITICAL: current recurring revenue evidence collapsed.
ideas.customer: Independent US residential moving companies using SmartMoving, roughly 2–10 trucks, one metro
ideas.wedge: SmartMoving-native lead delivery + smaller exclusive ZIP territories + done-for-you onboarding
ideas.why: High ARPU, tiny required customer count, identifiable buyers, direct-sales friendly, licensable inputs, measurable ROI
ideas.risk: The listing-to-booked-move conversion may be too weak to sustain repeatable ROI; incumbent could add the same integration wedge | 17 Oct critical update: zero active subscriptions now shown by TrustMRR; original 9.3 score is historical, not a current recommendation. Validate what caused the subscription collapse.

ideas.idea: White-label mobile app performance reporting for ASO and mobile-growth agencies
ideas.description: A reporting hub for agencies that manage multiple mobile-app clients. It connects each client's Apple App Store Connect, Google Play Console and selected acquisition sources, continuously normalizes performance data, and automatically produces branded client reports, portals and alerts instead of requiring analysts to rebuild dashboards or monthly decks.
ideas.incumbent: Easy App Reports by Beyond Analytics
ideas.traction: $3,474 MRR from 22 active subscriptions; $164,908 all-time revenue; 1-person bootstrapped team (TrustMRR, Aug 29 2026) | 17 Oct 2026 authenticated attempt: historical TrustMRR slug returned 'Startup not found'; current MRR and subscription count cannot be confirmed. This is NOT proof the business shut down.
ideas.customer: ASO and mobile-app growth agencies with ~5–50 active client apps and recurring retainers
ideas.wedge: Own the client-delivery layer: white-label portals, scheduled branded reports, KPI goals, annotations and commentary—rather than selling generic BI/data connectors
ideas.why: Verified low-customer-count B2B revenue, official/replicable data sources, enumerable agency buyers, recurring workflow pain, strong expansion pricing and a fast concierge validation path
ideas.risk: Agencies may already be satisfied with AppTweak/Appfigures/Looker Studio; Apple/Google permissions and source-report delays could make onboarding/support too heavy | 17 Oct: incumbent profile unavailable at historical slug; current traction not independently confirmed.

ideas.idea: AI Meta-ad comment-to-booking agent for home-improvement companies
ideas.description: A conversion agent for home-improvement companies already running Facebook and Instagram ads. It watches ad comments and DMs, hides obvious spam, answers approved buyer questions, detects high intent, qualifies prospects in private messages, books estimates, and writes the lead plus conversation context into the company's CRM.
ideas.traction: $8,363 MRR from 38 active subscriptions; $56,911 all-time revenue; Stripe-verified TrustMRR snapshot on 2026-09-07 | 17 Oct 2026 authenticated: $8,198.33 MRR; 37 active subscriptions; $9,876.30 revenue last 30d; $73,048.97 all-time; 30d MRR change -1.92%.
ideas.customer: US roofing companies with ~5–50 employees, meaningful Meta ad spend, and GoHighLevel/agency-managed lead workflows
ideas.wedge: Meta-first + roofing-first; turn paid-ad comments into qualified DMs and booked estimates in GoHighLevel, with done-for-you setup and revenue attribution
ideas.why: Strong verified ARPU with few incumbent customers, official/replicable platform APIs, easy-to-enumerate buyers, one job can pay for months of SaaS, and the core workflow can be concierge-validated before building broadly
ideas.risk: ManyChat/HighLevel/native Meta tools may already be good enough, or Meta permissions may constrain comment-to-DM automation; the thesis fails if qualified comments do not become incremental booked estimates | 17 Oct: incumbent describes DTC brand customers; roofing-first lead-to-booking wedge remains hypothetical. Slight 30-day MRR decline; validate Meta permissions and unit economics.

ideas.idea: Statement-first travel commission reconciliation and advisor-payout SaaS
ideas.description: A back-office tool for travel agencies that ingests the supplier commission statements they already receive as PDF, Excel, CSV, email or pasted text. It extracts booking and commission lines, matches them against the agency's expected bookings, flags missing or incorrect payments, calculates advisor splits, and produces a reconciled payout report and audit trail without requiring the agency to replace its CRM.
ideas.incumbent: Sion (with supporting validation from Toggle Travel, Wihemi Travel and Trip Ledger)
ideas.traction: Sion acquired by Bilt for $30M on 11 Mar 2026; Sion says 8,000+ advisors and $7B+ booking revenue managed. Toggle starts at $350/mo; Wihemi $169/mo. JourneyFuse separately shows ~$6.38k verified MRR / 300 subscriptions on TrustMRR. | 17 Oct 2026 authenticated: adjacent JourneyFuse now $9,336 MRR / 467 subscriptions; $18,669.18 revenue last 30d; +29.27% MRR change. Does not directly validate commission reconciliation.
ideas.customer: US independent travel agencies and small host agencies with ~10–75 advisors, roughly $2M–$30M annual booking volume, multiple suppliers, and manual/spreadsheet-heavy commission reconciliation.
ideas.wedge: Statement-first instead of CRM/GDS-first: upload supplier statements plus a simple booking export, reconcile automatically with a human-review exception queue, then add only the integrations repeated customers actually demand.
ideas.why: Exceptionally strong proof of willingness to pay and strategic value, easy-to-identify B2B buyers, recurring financial workflow, $300–$1,000+ plausible ARPU, and a concierge MVP that can validate extraction/matching before building deep integrations.
ideas.risk: Statement variability and ambiguous booking matching could force customer-specific integrations and turn the product into a services-heavy back-office implementation; incumbents may already solve enough of the problem. | JourneyFuse revenue proves willingness to pay for broader agency CRM, not specifically the proposed supplier-statement matching and payouts.

ideas.idea: Event-triggered group-booking prospecting for independent hotels
ideas.description: A revenue-generation SaaS for independent hotels that watches public event signals such as sports tournaments, conferences and festivals, identifies organizers likely to need room blocks, finds decision-maker contacts, and launches personalized outreach. Interested group-booking leads are qualified and routed into the hotel's existing sales workflow, with attribution from event signal through booked room revenue.
ideas.traction: TrustMRR: $2,545 MRR from 7 active subscriptions; $3,944 last 30 days; $25,226 all-time revenue; Stripe-verified, updated Sep 20 2026 | 17 Oct 2026 authenticated: HotelHero.ai $3,042 MRR / 8 subs; $2,988.46 revenue last 30d; $28,214.13 lifetime; MRR change +19.53%, 30d collected revenue -24.23%.
ideas.customer: Independent US hotels/small groups with ~40–150 rooms, limited in-house group sales, near sports complexes or recurring tournaments
ideas.wedge: Productize only event-triggered group-sales prospecting, starting with sports tournaments; public event signals → organizer outreach → warm lead handoff, rather than a broad hotel marketing agency
ideas.why: Very high implied ARPU with only 7 incumbent subscriptions, tiny founder audience/DR, measurable room-revenue ROI, enumerable buyers, and a concierge MVP that can be sold before deep integrations
ideas.risk: Public event/contact data may be fragmented, organizers may already use housing partners, and proactive outreach may fail to produce incremental booked room blocks | 17 Oct: business appears to mix hotel remote sales/marketing services; revenue may reflect labour-intensive services rather than a transferable self-serve SaaS.

ideas.idea: Shopify fulfillment-savings autopilot for high-volume brands
ideas.description: A Shopify app that briefly holds eligible orders, detects same-customer/same-address purchases, lets shoppers add or correct items, consolidates eligible orders into one fulfillment, and then releases the finalized order to the warehouse or 3PL. It reports verified shipping cost saved, support work avoided, and incremental post-purchase revenue.
ideas.incumbent: Mergify (with OrderEditing.com and Triom as supporting validation)
ideas.traction: Flippa listing reports $12.9k MRR, 3,000+ active users and 4% churn; Shopify App Store independently shows a live Built for Shopify app with current paid plans.
ideas.customer: Shopify brands doing roughly 2,000–20,000 orders/month, especially launch/drop or repeat-purchase brands using a 3PL.
ideas.wedge: 3PL-first hold/merge/release workflow plus customer add-ons and a verified dollars-saved dashboard; sell fulfillment savings rather than generic order merging.
ideas.why: Direct measurable ROI, data-verified marketplace traction, reproducible Shopify distribution, normal SaaS engineering, and a read-only audit can validate demand before risky order mutations are built.
ideas.risk: Duplicate-order incidence may be too low, or 3PL/Shopify race conditions may make safe automated consolidation harder than expected.

ideas.idea: WhatsApp-first materials request and purchase-order coordination for UK electrical subcontractors
ideas.description: A site foreman sends a voice note, photo or short message listing materials needed for a specific job. The software turns it into a structured request, routes it to the office for approval, emails a purchase order to the firm's existing supplier, and matches delivery photos and outstanding items to each job. It replaces scattered WhatsApp messages, phone calls and spreadsheets without replacing accounting or supplier systems.
ideas.traction: Starter Story founder interview (Feb 2025) reports ~$50k/month, started 2021, one founder; current SubBase website and independent Capterra reviews corroborate the product/workflow, but current revenue/customer count is not independently verified.
ideas.customer: UK commercial electrical subcontractors with ~10–60 field operatives and 5–25 simultaneous sites, currently requesting materials through WhatsApp, phone and spreadsheets.
ideas.wedge: Opt-in 1:1 WhatsApp voice/photo material requisitions + UK electrical item aliases + human-approved supplier POs and delivery proof; no ERP migration, no supplier marketplace.
ideas.why: Founder-reported established vertical SaaS revenue, independent complaints around mobile/electrical catalog, clear reachable trade niche, recurring operational pain and a paid concierge validation path.
ideas.risk: Foremen may resist workflow changes; SKU matching and WhatsApp/API constraints could force bespoke onboarding or make the workflow unreliable.
